Luis Walter Alvarez is a physicist. Alvarez devised a set of experiments to observe K-electron capture in radioactive nuclei, predicted by the beta decay theory but never before observed.
Pick the chemist from these four.
What is the atomic number of Lithium?
Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.
In what year was Pope Benedict XVI born?
Pope Benedict XVI: Following his resignation, he chose to be known as "pope emeritus", a title he held until his death on 31 December 2022.
In what year was Iodine discovered?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
In what year was Nickel discovered?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Magnesium sulfate: Pfizer. It is a white crystalline solid, soluble in water.
In which country is Blood orange?
Blood orange: Italy. The blood orange is a variety of orange with crimson, near blood-colored flesh.
Who is credited with discovering Caesium?
Caesium: Robert Bunsen. Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
Who is credited with discovering Nobelium?
Nobelium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
Who is credited with discovering Silicon?
Silicon: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.

Sometimes called a nerve impulse or 'spike,' this rapid rise and fall of voltage across a cell membrane ripples to neighboring spots and fires in neurons, muscle cells, and even some plant cells. What is it?
Action potential (also known as a nerve impulse or "spike" when in a neuron) is a series of quick changes in voltage across a cell membrane.

With roughly 370 million individuals, this migratory thrush outnumbers red-winged blackbirds and starlings across its home continent, despite being misnamed after an unrelated European species — what is it?
American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.
This Portuguese economist-turned-dictator ruled as head of government from 1932 to 1968, rebranding his authoritarian regime as the corporatist 'New State.' Who is he?
António de Oliveira Salazar (28 April 1889 - 27 July 1970) was a Portuguese dictator, academic, and economist who served as President of the Council of Ministers of Portugal from 1932 to 1968.
This American psychologist developed the philosophy of radical behaviorism and pioneered operant conditioning while a longtime professor at Harvard — who is he?
B. F. Skinner (March 20, 1904 - August 18, 1990) was an American psychologist, behaviorist, inventor, and social philosopher.

First flickering to life in octocorals some 540 million years ago and evolving independently at least 94 separate times, this glow is sometimes borrowed from symbiotic bacteria — what is the phenomenon?
Bioluminescence is the production of light by an organism as the result of a chemiluminescence reaction.

David Attenborough called this English particle physicist the natural successor for the BBC's scientific programming, thanks to shows like The Infinite Monkey Cage and his Wonders of... series — who is he?
Brian Cox (physicist) (born 3 March 1968) is an English physicist and musician.
Nine to ten times as massive as the Sun and expanded to 71 times its radius, this blue-loop giant in the constellation Carina ranks second only to Sirius in night-sky brightness — which star?
Canopus is the brightest star in the southern constellation of Carina and the second-brightest star in the night sky.
Domesticated from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia about 8,000 years ago, this social bird now numbers over 26.5 billion worldwide — what is it?
Chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.

Lacking the sucking mouthparts of aphids, this chewing-mouthed insect is considered one of the most primitive alive — and a famous few of its 4,600 species became notorious household pests. What is it?
Cockroach (or roaches) are insects belonging to the order Blattodea (Blattaria).
This is the capacity to produce novel, valuable ideas or works — whether an invention, a scientific theory, a joke, or a piece of jewelry — through the exercise of imagination — what's the capacity?
Creativity is the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas or works through the exercise of imagination.

Named from the Latin word for 'finger' because of its tubular, spike-borne flowers, this genus of about 20 European and West Asian species was reclassified into a new plant family in 2001 — what is it commonly called?
Digitalis (or) is a genus of about 20 species of herbaceous perennial plants, shrubs, and biennials, commonly called foxgloves.
Sometimes occurring spontaneously during sleep as a nocturnal emission, this process involves the discharge of semen through the urethra — what is it called?
Ejaculation is the discharge of semen (the ejaculate; normally containing sperm) from the penis through the urethra.

This simple hydrocarbon gas, the simplest member of a class called alkenes, is the most-produced organic compound on Earth by tonnage, and is the primary building block of a common plastic — what is it?
Ethylene (IUPAC name: ethene) is a hydrocarbon which has the formula C2H4 or H2C=CH2.
Encompassing everything from oral tales and proverbs to festival rituals and traditional building styles, what term describes the shared expressive culture of a group?
Folklore is the body of expressive culture shared by a particular group of people, culture or subculture.
The largest of four living anteater species, this terrestrial mammal of Central and South America is known for its elongated snout, bushy tail, and long foreclaws. What is it?
Giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) is an insectivorous mammal native to Central and South America.
What protein filament, grown from follicles in the skin's dermis layer and composed mainly of alpha-keratin, is one of the defining characteristics of mammals?
Hair is a protein filament that grows from follicles found in the dermis.

Known taxonomically as Lonicera, this genus of 158 species of arching shrubs and twining vines is native to northern latitudes worldwide, though one of its Asian members has become a notorious invasive pest — what's the plant?
Honeysuckle are arching shrubs or twining vines in the genus Lonicera of the family Caprifoliaceae.
Supplied by the lumbar spinal nerves and part of the femoral nerve, this fused pair of abdominal and thigh muscles is the body's strongest hip flexor — what is it called?
Iliopsoas (from Latin ile 'groin' and Ancient Greek (ps) 'muscles of the loins') refers to the joined psoas major and the iliacus muscles.
This French mathematician of algebraic topology and number theory pulled off a rare double: the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly fifty years later, the very first Abel Prize. Who was he?
Jean-Pierre Serre (born 15 September 1926) is a French mathematician who has made contributions to algebraic topology, algebraic geometry and algebraic number theory.
Native to eastern and southern Africa, this flowering shrub is the sole species in its genus and has a documented history of cultivation dating back to Ethiopia's Harar region. Name the plant?
Khat (Catha edulis), also known as Bushman's tea, especially in South Africa, is a species of flowering plant in the family Celastraceae, and the sole species in genus Catha.

This group of blood cancers typically begins in the bone marrow and produces abnormal blood cells called blasts. Symptoms include bleeding, bruising, bone pain, and fever due to a lack of normal blood cells — what is this disease?
Leukemia (also spelled leukaemia) is a group of blood cancers that usually begin in the bone marrow and produce high numbers of abnormal blood cells.
Its name is Latin for 'wolf,' and this autoimmune disease cycles between flares and remission, often announcing itself with a red rash across the face — what is it?
Lupus (SLE), is an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissue in many parts of the body.
Number theory, algebra, geometry, analysis and set theory are all branches of this field, which leans on logical reasoning and proof to study abstract concepts — what is it?
Mathematics is a field of knowledge concerned with abstract concepts such as numbers, geometric shapes, sets, functions, and probabilities.
First flown by the Soviet Air Force in 1968 and still in Russian production today, this medium chopper carries the NATO reporting name 'Hip' — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-8 is a family of medium twin-turbine helicopters, originally designed by the Soviet Central Aerohydrodynamic Institute (TsAGI) in the 1960s and introduced into the Soviet Air Force in 1968.
Unlike its cousin hemoglobin, this protein binds oxygen without cooperative binding and only shows up in a human's bloodstream after muscle injury — which protein?
Myoglobin (symbol Mb or MB) is an iron- and oxygen-binding protein found in the cardiac and skeletal muscle tissue of vertebrates in general and in almost all mammals.
The smallest of its type, this Canadian gun dog has webbed feet and lures waterfowl to shore with playful antics before fetching them from the water — which breed is it?
Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized gun dog bred primarily for hunting.

Created by Danish-Canadian programmer Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993 and released in 1995, this general-purpose scripting language was originally short for 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym — name the language?
PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
This class of compounds is defined by a direct single bond between two oxygen atoms, denoted R−O−O−R — what are they called?
Peroxide are a group of molecules with the structure ROOR, where each R represents a radical (a portion of a complete molecule; not a free radical) and the O's are single oxygen atoms.
Its common name is shared with an unrelated tropical fruit, but this genus of roughly 200 herbaceous species — also called fleaworts — belongs to the family Plantaginaceae. Which genus?
Plantago is a genus of about 200 species of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae, commonly called plantains or fleaworts.

Derived enzymatically from a fatty acid found in nearly every tissue of the body, this class of lipid compounds produces diverse hormone-like effects despite not being true hormones — what are they called?
Prostaglandin (PG) are a group of physiologically active lipid compounds that have diverse hormone-like effects in animals.
Along with his two brothers, this American physician-turned-businessman acquired the pharmaceutical company behind OxyContin, later linked to the U.S. opioid crisis — who is he?
Raymond Sackler (February 16, 1920 - July 17, 2017) was an American physician and businessman.

Named after the naturalist who first documented it, this highly venomous South Asian snake is known for an extremely painful bite and ranks among the region's 'Big Four' dangerous species — what snake is it?
Russell's viper (Daboia russelii) is a species of highly venomous snake in the family Viperidae.

Native only to groves on California's Sierra Nevada slopes, this conifer species includes the largest trees on Earth by volume, though fewer than 80,000 remain and it's now listed as endangered — what's the species?

Sequoiadendron giganteum (also known as the giant sequoia, giant redwood, Sierra redwood or Wellingtonia) is a species of coniferous tree, classified in the family Cupressaceae in the subfamily Sequoioideae.
This Polish-American Gestalt psychologist insisted 'most social acts lose meaning if isolated' — a credo that shaped his famous experiments on conformity and impression formation. Who was he?
Solomon Asch (September 14, 1907 - February 20, 1996) was a Polish-American Gestalt psychologist and pioneer in social psychology.
This small nocturnal marsupial sails between trees on membranes stretched from wrist to ankle, and its Latin name translates as 'short-headed rope-dancer' — what animal is it?
Sugar glider (Petaurus breviceps) is a small, omnivorous, arboreal, and nocturnal gliding possum.
This vast domain of human practice — divided into visual, literary, and performing branches — lets people transmit values, ideas, and experiences across generations. What is it?
The arts are a vast range of human practices involving creative expression, storytelling, and cultural participation.
Caused by a single-celled parasite and often symptom-free, this common STI can be diagnosed by examining vaginal fluid under a microscope or with a DNA test — what is it?
Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.
This broad category of creative disciplines spans painting, sculpture, photography, and architecture, and includes applied fields like industrial and fashion design — what do we call it?
Visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture.
This Russian political activist and economist, described as the 'first lady' of her country's opposition, vowed to continue her late husband's work after fleeing into exile. Who is she?
Yulia Navalnaya (ne Abrosimova; born 24 July 1976) is a Russian political activist and economist.
This protrusion in the neck, formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage around the larynx, becomes more prominent in most men during puberty — what is it?
Adam's apple: Feature of the neck. The Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.

This organic functional group, structured R−CH=O and alternatively called a formyl group when isolated from its side chain, appears throughout biologically and technologically important chemicals — what is it?
Aldehyde: Organic compound containing the functional group R–CH=O.
Sold under the brand name Norvasc, this long-acting calcium channel blocker treats high blood pressure and variant angina by relaxing and widening the arteries — what's the drug?
Amlodipine: Medication against high blood pressure.
Caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis, its skin form starts as a small blister that becomes a painless ulcer with a telltale black center — what infection is this?
Anthrax: Infection caused by Bacillus anthracis bacteria. The skin form presents with a small blister with surrounding swelling that often turns into a painless ulcer with a black center.
Literally meaning "hardening of the arteries," this umbrella term covers vascular disorders marked by abnormal thickening and loss of elasticity in artery walls — what is it called?
Arteriosclerosis: Thickening, hardening and loss of elasticity of the walls of arteries.
Sold as Zithromax, this antibiotic tackles strep throat, pneumonia and traveler's diarrhea — but its tendency to cause QT prolongation keeps doctors watchful of the heart. Which drug is it?
Azithromycin: Antibiotic. It is administered by mouth, into a vein, or as topical treatment for the eye.
A likely hybrid of lemon and a bitter citrus relative, this fragrant fruit flavors tea, snus, and perfume, though it can heighten skin's sensitivity to sunlight — which fruit?
Credited with kicking off the Jet Age, this swept-wing quadjet airliner entered regular passenger service with Pan Am in October 1958 — which aircraft?

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered as a Cambridge PhD student in 1962 — then, in the 1970s, took up Transcendental Meditation and pursued ideas beyond mainstream science. Who is he?
Its dihydrate form is the mineral gypsum and its dehydrated cousin is bassanite; sparingly soluble, it causes permanent hardness in water — which inorganic salt is this?
Calcium sulfate: Chemical derived from gypsum used in food and industry.
A nerve compression syndrome caused when the median nerve in the wrist becomes compressed, causing numbness and tingling in the thumb and fingers. What is this condition?
Carpal tunnel syndrome: Compression of the median nerve in the wrist. It can also be measured with electrodiagnostic tests.
India's third lunar mission carried a lander named Vikram and a rover, both replacing equivalents lost when the previous mission crashed on landing. What was the rover called?

Chandrayaan-3 is the third mission in ISRO's Chandrayaan lunar-exploration programme, consisting of the lander Vikram and the rover Pragyan, replacements for the equivalents on Chandrayaan-2, which crashed on landing.
In this chronic liver condition, healthy tissue is replaced by scar tissue and regenerative nodules, choking blood flow and causing portal hypertension — what is it called?
Cirrhosis: Chronic disease of the liver, characterized by fibrosis.
In this prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a person cannot be awakened, shows no normal sleep-wake cycle, and may even be induced deliberately during general anesthesia — what is it?
Coma: State of unconsciousness. The person may experience respiratory and circulatory problems due to the body's inability to maintain normal bodily functions.
Smelling of vanilla but tasting bitter, which plant compound isn't itself an anticoagulant, though its derivatives inspired the blood-thinning drug warfarin?
This Zambian-born economist turned heads with four New York Times bestsellers, including "Dead Aid," which argues that foreign aid actually holds Africa back. Which author and life peer is it?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo: Zambian-born economist (born February 1969)
Known for feigning death when cornered, which genus of cat-sized marsupials includes the only marsupial species found north of Mexico?
Didelphis: Genus of marsupials. The six species in the genus Didelphis, commonly known as Large American opossums, are members of the opossum order, Didelphimorphia.
Nicknamed 'Viking disease,' this hand condition — first surgically treated in 1831 by the surgeon it's named after — permanently curls the ring finger inward. What is it?
Dupuytren's contracture: Medical condition featuring permanent bending of fingers.
A Swedish scientist and inventor until, at 53, dreams and visions sent him into a spiritual phase, this polymath became best known for his 1758 book on the afterlife, Heaven and Hell — who was he?
Emanuel Swedenborg: Swedish scientist, philosopher, and theologian (1688–1772)
With a sweet smell like pear drops, this colorless solvent turns up in nail-polish remover and is used to decaffeinate tea and coffee. What is it?
Named after a 19th-century English physicist, this SI unit measures a material's ability to store electrical charge, equal to one coulomb per volt — what is it?
Farad: SI unit of electric capacitance.
Patented in 1962 and sold under a brand name synonymous with 'roofies,' this benzodiazepine is notoriously linked to date-rape drug use — what is it?
Flunitrazepam: Benzodiazepine sedative. Flunitrazepam, sold under the brand name Rohypnol among others, is a benzodiazepine used to treat severe insomnia and assist with anesthesia.
Born in Pisa in 1564, this Italian polymath has been crowned the father of observational astronomy and the scientific method — and was among the earliest tinkerers to build a thermoscope. Who is he?
Galileo Galilei: Italian physicist and astronomer (1564–1642)

This Italian friar and cosmological theorist proposed that stars were distant suns with their own planets, and was tried for heresy by the Roman Inquisition for insisting the universe is infinite — who was he?
Giordano Bruno: Italian Dominican friar, philosopher and mathematician (1548–1600)
This junctional area between the torso and thigh, where the lower abdominal wall meets the leg, is commonly strained in a familiar sports injury — what is it called?
Groin: Area between the torso and the thigh. In human anatomy, the groin, also known as the inguinal region or iliac region, is the junctional area between the torso and the thigh.

In 2018 this Chinese biophysicist announced the world's first gene-edited human babies — twin girls modified for HIV resistance — which got him onto Time's influential list and fired from his university. Who was he?
This academic discipline studies the methods, sources, and interpretive approaches historians use when writing about the past — what's it called?
Historiography: Study of the methods used by historians.
Defined as a blood level above 5.5 mmol/L, this elevated-potassium condition can trigger a dangerous heart rhythm and even cardiac arrest — what is it called?
Hyperkalemia: Excess potassium in the blood. Normal potassium levels are between 3.5 and 5.0 mmol/L (3.5 and 5.0 mEq/L) with levels above 5.5 mmol/L defined as hyperkalemia.

ISO 56000:2020 defines it as "a new or changed entity, realizing or redistributing value" — but the everyday version is the practical implementation of ideas, the cousin of invention focused on newness, improvement, and the spread of technologies. What's the word?
Innovation: Practical implementation of improvements. Innovation is the practical implementation of ideas that result in the creation or improvements of goods or services.
Mentored by Louis Leakey, this English primatologist spent six decades at Gombe and revealed that chimpanzees use tools and form lasting social bonds — who was she?
Named the type genus of the walnut family, this group of deciduous trees produces the walnuts eaten worldwide, with China responsible for half the global supply — which genus?
Juglans: Genus of trees. Walnut trees are any species of tree in the plant genus Juglans, the type genus of the family Juglandaceae, the seeds of which are referred to as walnuts.
Native to southern China and roughly the size of a large olive, which citrus fruit closely resembles a tiny orange and is famously cold-hardy?
Kumquat: Species of small fruit-bearing tree.
Often beginning in the bone marrow, this group of cancers floods the body with immature 'blast' cells, bringing easy bruising, bone pain, and frequent infections — what is it?
Also called dragon's eye, this tropical fruit tree from the soapberry family produces fruit similar to lychee but with a milder aroma, and is native to Southeast Asia and southern China — what is it?
Longan: Species of tropical fruit-bearing tree.

Discovered in 2005 by the same Palomar team whose haul of big, icy Kuiper-belt bodies pushed astronomers to demote Pluto in 2006, this fourth-largest dwarf planet has a methane-frosted, tholin-reddened surface — what is it?
Makemake: Dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.

First flown in August 1970 and introduced by American Airlines the following year, this trijet wide-body aircraft has two underwing engines and a third mounted at the base of its tail fin — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas DC-10: Wide-body three-engine airliner.
Sold under the brand name Medrol, this synthetic steroid can trigger iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome if not carefully tapered after high-dose use for acute flares — name the drug?

An Egyptian-born civil engineer and architect who studied in Cairo and Germany, at 33 he was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta: Egyptian terrorist and 9/11 hijacker (1968–2001)
This autoimmune disease attacks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, often causing drooping eyelids, double vision, and difficulty swallowing — which condition?
Myasthenia gravis: Autoimmune disease resulting in skeletal muscle weakness.
Also known in everyday speech as 'brain surgery,' this medical specialty treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and the entire nervous system — what is it called?
Neurosurgery: Medical specialty of disorders which affect any portion of the nervous system.
Thriving in the cool, wet summers of Northwest Europe, this hardy cereal grass tolerates low-nutrient, acidic soil and is dominated globally by Canadian and Russian production?
This fluid-filled sac that forms within the ovary is usually harmless and often tied to ovulation, appearing as a follicular or corpus luteum type — what is it?
Ovarian cyst: Fluid-filled sac in the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
He earned a PhD in physics from Cambridge for the first-ever thesis on quantum mechanics, then shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger — who is he?
Turning colorless in acid and a fuchsia pink in base, this phthalein dye is a favorite indicator for acid-base titrations — what is it?
Phenolphthalein: pH indicator that turns pink in basic solution.
Widely planted along London's streets as a hybrid variety, this tree genus includes the sycamores of North America and can tower up to 50 meters — which genus?
Platanus: Genus of flowering plants constituting the family Platanaceae.

Arising over 60 million years ago from small tree-dwellers, this order favored big brains, binocular color vision and opposable thumbs to grasp among the branches — and it includes lemurs and apes — what is it?
Primate: Order of mammals. New primate species continue to be discovered: over 25 species were described in the 2000s, 36 in the 2010s, and six in the 2020s.
Usually caused by E. coli spreading up the urinary tract, this kidney infection typically brings fever and flank tenderness, and can be prevented by urinating after sex — what condition is it?
Pyelonephritis: Inflammation of the kidney. It is typically due to a bacterial infection, most commonly Escherichia coli.
From a startled jump to a cat automatically reorienting itself mid-fall, this involuntary, split-second reaction runs through the nervous system without needing conscious thought — what's it called?
Reflex: Automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus.
Usually hidden underground, this plant organ anchors it in place while drawing in water and nutrients — what is it?
Root: Basal organ of a vascular plant.

With ears set low to detect prey moving underground and furry paw soles that insulate against scorching ground, this small desert feline was first described in the Algerian Sahara in 1858 — which animal?
Sand cat: Small wild cat species (Felis margarita)

Nicknamed the 'last Soviet citizen' for being aboard Mir when the USSR dissolved, this cosmonaut flew six missions and helped connect the first Russian and American modules of a space station — who is he?
Sergei Krikalev: Soviet and Russian cosmonaut (born 1958)
This big cat of the genus Panthera prowls the alpine zones of Central and South Asia at elevations of 3,000 to 4,500 meters, from the Himalayas to southern Siberia — what is it?
Snow leopard: Species of large felid.

Named after the patron saint of sailors, this luminous blue or violet glow appears around masts, spires, or aircraft during a strong electric field and can warn of an imminent lightning strike — what is this phenomenon called?
St. Elmo's fire: Luminous plasma created in an electric field.
Designed by R. J. Mitchell with a distinctive elliptical wing and sunken rivets for minimal drag, this was the only British fighter kept in continuous production throughout World War II — what is it?
Supermarine Spitfire: British single-seat WWII fighter aircraft.
Known as the barn funnel weaver in North America and simply the house spider in Europe, this species belongs to the funnel-web family Agelenidae — which arachnid?
Shaped like a butterfly and sitting in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland secretes hormones that regulate metabolic rate — which gland is it?
Thyroid: Endocrine gland in the neck. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi).
This ester of glycerol and three fatty acids is the main constituent of body fat and a major component of human skin oils — what is it?
Triglyceride: Any ester of glycerol having all three hydroxyl groups esterified with fatty acids.

With co-researcher James Cronin, this American nuclear physicist won the 1980 Nobel for a 1964 K-meson experiment proving certain subatomic reactions aren't indifferent to time — discovering CP violation. Who was he?
Val Logsdon Fitch: American nuclear physicist. Born on a cattle ranch near Merriman, Nebraska, Fitch was drafted into the U.S.
Botanically a berry called a 'pepo,' this trailing vine's fruit comes in over 1,000 varieties and has a rind that's actually edible once cooked — what is it?
Spread mainly by the Aedes aegypti mosquito, this viral illness can cause a brief recovery before a relapse brings liver damage and jaundice — what disease is it?
Yellow fever: Viral disease. In most cases, symptoms include fever, chills, loss of appetite, nausea, muscle pains—particularly in the back—and headaches.
Gadolinium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for gadolinium is Gd. Gadolinium is a chemical element; it has symbol Gd and atomic number 64.
